Drove all four navigation items - see 01-home-row-open and the URLs recorded there. 'Remove the local install' on nodehealth opened the confirmation modal ("This Rancher stops loading nodehealth: its UIPlugin is deleted...") and Cancel closed it; I did not press 'Remove it' because deleting a shared UIPlugin would break other agents' verifications, and kubectl confirms the nodehealth UIPlugin is still installed.

verdicts.defect: pages/extensions.vue line 635: the Review button is @click.stop="open(row.name)", which pushes EDITOR_ROUTE. It should push REVIEW_ROUTE with params { extension: row.name }, the same as onRowAction's 'review' branch.

verdicts.evidence: All four extensions currently in the cluster were created here, and each shows the icon-ai sparkle plus "Created here · no repo yet". To exercise the repo-backed branch I temporarily set the demo extension's barn.rancher.io/source annotation to github:verify-01home/demo#audit-01home (a value keyed to this audit): its row then rendered the icon-github mark and "verify-01home/demo · audit-01home", read live from the configmap annotation. I restored the annotation to 'base' immediately afterwards and confirmed with kubectl that it is back.

Every name cell renders a second muted line and each one matched the row's real state: base "1 change waiting for your review" (git status in the pod: 1 entry), nodehealth "2 changes waiting for your review" (git status: 2 entries), demo "Compiling - the preview reloads when it finishes" (deployment scaled 0/0), q11probe "On main, nothing uncommitted" (an extension another agent created mid-run, ready with a clean tree). A published-but-clean row would read "Released as v<x> to this Rancher".

Three distinct values, all cross-checked. nodehealth reads "catalog · v0.1.0" and `kubectl get uiplugins -A` shows nodehealth 0.1.0 installed in cattle-ui-plugin-system. base and q11probe read "local (preview)": their deployments are 1/1 and neither has a UIPlugin. demo reads "-": its deployment is 0/0 and it has no UIPlugin. So published-to-catalog, preview-only and nowhere are each distinguished from live readings.

The cell renders a real relative time, correctly formatted and correctly derived: base "1 day ago" against git log -1 --format=%cI = 2026-08-21T22:37:47Z, nodehealth "2 hours ago" against 2026-08-22T22:25:12Z, demo "-" (pod down, no reading). But the value is the last COMMIT, not the last change. base's working tree has an uncommitted BRIEF.md whose mtime in the pod is 2026-08-22T23:40:00Z - 43 minutes before I read the page - and the row's own subtitle says "1 change waiting for your review", yet the Last change cell says "1 day ago".
verdicts.defect: extensionDetail() (extensions.ts ~line 1650) sources lastChange from `git log -1 --format=%cI`, so editing a file never moves the column; only committing does. A column headed "Last change" next to a subtitle announcing uncommitted changes should take the newer of the last commit and the newest working-tree mtime. I did not drive the 'just now' transition because that would require committing in a pod other verifiers are reading.

verdicts.evidence: Sorts on the timestamp, not the rendered string, and I proved it rather than assumed it. With the real data the two orderings coincide, so I shifted only Date.now() forward 24h in the page (Date.parse of the ISO timestamps is untouched) so that the older extension renders the LATER-sorting string: base (older) rendered "2 days ago" and nodehealth (newer) rendered "1 day ago". First click gave aria-sort=descending and the order nodehealth "1 day ago", base "2 days ago", demo "-" - i.e. newest first. A string sort would have put "2 days ago" on top. Second click gave ascending and the exact reverse (demo "-", base, nodehealth). The header carries a chevron that turns from chevronDown to chevronUp and gets the --on treatment.

Click 1: aria-sort=ascending, order base, demo, nodehealth. Click 2: aria-sort=descending, order nodehealth, demo, base. Click 3 returned to ascending. Caret flips chevronUp/chevronDown and the title attribute reads "Sorted ascending, click to reverse" / "Sorted descending, click to reverse".

Sorts on the underlying target, not the cell text. Click 1 (ascending): nodehealth "catalog · v0.1.0", base "local (preview)", demo "-" - installed first, previewing second, nowhere last. A string sort would have put "-" first, not last. Click 2 (descending) gave the exact reverse: demo "-", base, nodehealth. Click 3 restored the first order, and aria-sort tracked ascending/descending each time.

With every row 'Created here' the sort has nothing to separate, so I temporarily gave the demo extension the source annotation github:verify-01home/demo#audit-01home (restored afterwards, see 01-home-row-source). Click 1: aria-sort=ascending, order base, nodehealth (both 'Created here', which sort as the empty string and group together), then demo "verify-01home/demo · audit-01home". Click 2: aria-sort=descending, demo first then base, nodehealth. The caret gets the --on treatment on the Source header and the direction indicator flips.

Click 1: aria-sort=ascending, order base:Unsaved, nodehealth:Unsaved, demo:Building, q11probe:Live. That is the attention order in STATE_ORDER (failed, unsaved, building, live, published, draft) with the name breaking the Unsaved tie - not alphabetical on the badge word, which would have been Building, Live, Unsaved. Click 2: aria-sort=descending, exact reverse (q11probe:Live, demo:Building, base, nodehealth). Click 3 back to ascending.

Every row leads with an .s-badge pill and each one is a live reading, cross-checked. base and nodehealth: "Unsaved" (s-badge--warning, #c9a227 on #fdf6e3) - git status in each pod shows 1 and 2 uncommitted entries. demo: "Building" (s-badge--info, #3d98d3 on #deebf7) - `kubectl -n barn get deploy` shows barn-demo-extension 0/0. q11probe, an extension another agent created 55 seconds earlier: "Live" (s-badge--success, #3e8c4f on #ebf4ec) - deployment 1/1, clean tree, and no UIPlugin, so not Published. nodehealth is the one row with a UIPlugin (v0.1.0) and it correctly badges Unsaved rather than Published because uncommitted work outranks publication. All six tone tokens resolve to distinct real colours on the page. Two caveats, neither a hardcoded value: I could not observe Published or Failed with real data during the run, and stateOf() can only ever return building/unsaved/published/live - 'failed' and 'draft' are unreachable from this screen except as the pre-enrichment default.
